bio.p1: Since 2022 I've built web apps in Vue.js and TypeScript professionally, first at Euronet Worldwide on the XE and Ria money transfer apps. On XE I was one of the main developers on the migration from Vue 2 and Vuex to Vue 3, Pinia and TypeScript, in a team of 10.
bio.p2: In 2026 I co-founded Fair Assistant and built it with AI coding agents: an Android app on Google Play (about three months from first commit to public release), a Nuxt team dashboard, a Nuxt website in 22 languages and a Node.js and PostgreSQL API.
bio.p3: I'm looking for a senior frontend or full-stack role, remote from Belgrade (employment, EOR or B2B contract) or hybrid in Belgrade.

fa.title: Technical Lead and Co-founder
fa.intro: Business card scanner for trade show exhibitors, live on Google Play with in-app purchases.

bullets.lead: First commit to public Google Play release took about three months. I set the product and architecture direction and ran the work through parallel Claude Code agents. Specs and API contracts came first, and nothing was merged without code review and passing tests.
bullets.android: Shipped the Android app in Kotlin and Jetpack Compose (Room, CameraX, on-device ML Kit text recognition, Google Play Billing), with over 2,000 unit tests.
bullets.web: Designed the 10 screens of the team dashboard (app.fairassistant.com) and built it as a Nuxt 4 single-page app in TypeScript, with Playwright end-to-end tests against a mock API. I also redesigned fairassistant.com in Nuxt with server-side rendering: 22 languages, a trade fair directory and live Google Play prices for 174 regions.
bullets.api: Built the licensing and payments API in TypeScript (Node.js, Fastify, PostgreSQL) from an OpenAPI 3.1 contract. It verifies Google Play purchases, signs license tokens and has nearly 1,000 Vitest tests. In production since September 2026.

details.summary: Encryption and AI card reading, in more detail
details.sync: Contact sync is end-to-end encrypted. Contacts are encrypted with AES-256-GCM on the phone, the key stays in the user's Google Drive app data, and team keys travel only inside a QR invite. The server stores only ciphertext and metadata.
details.teamKey: The phone passes the team key to the dashboard through a QR code and an ECDH P-256 key exchange. The dashboard decrypts contacts in a Web Worker and never stores them unencrypted.
details.ai: AI card reading runs on Gemini vision models with structured JSON output. Answers were coming back with 3 of 12 fields. I traced it to the alphabetical field order of the response schema and fixed it with an explicit property order. Answers now return 11 or 12 of the 12 fields, in 1.4 to 2.7 seconds.
